findings:
🔵 [encode-non-ascii-key] CUT/FOLLOW-UP `_ts_encode_key` uses `printf '%02X' "'$c"`, which yields a codepoint (possibly more than 2 hex digits) for a non-ASCII subsection character, while `_ts_decode_key` reads exactly 2 digits; drift on such a key is still detected and fails the run, but the DRIFT line and restore target a mis-decoded key. Excluded: the spec's named cases (slash, percent, URL keys) are ASCII and round-trip correctly; encode per byte under LC_ALL=C later.
🔵 [valueless-key-restore] CUT/FOLLOW-UP `_ts_explode_config_z` stores the key name as the value for a valueless record (`key\0` with no newline), and `_ts_restore_key_from_file` passes values starting with `-` to `git config --add` without protection, so restoring those two shapes can write a wrong value or silently skip. Excluded: only reached when such a key drifts, the run still fails with the key named, and the spec does not require it.
🔵 [worktree-path-whitespace] CUT/FOLLOW-UP `_ts_extract_diff_names` prints `$1` with default awk field splitting for worktree detail lines, so a worktree path containing spaces is truncated in the WARNING; `sed 's/^\t//'` also relies on GNU sed. Excluded: warning-only cosmetics, no sha or value can be printed, return code unaffected; use `awk -F'\t'` and `$'s/^\t//'` later.
🔵 [encoded-name-length] CUT/FOLLOW-UP an encoded key longer than NAME_MAX (255 bytes) still fails the `>>"$dir/$enc"` write and is dropped. Excluded: needs a key far longer than the URL-style keys the spec names; hash long names later.
